critical_evidence.quote_or_cell: Supplier may continue at risk on a letter of intent, capped in value, while approvals are pending.
critical_evidence.why_wrong: This permits supplier activity under a commercial authorization before required approvals are complete, without defining who approves the letter of intent or excluding implementation of unapproved design changes. A value cap and supplier acceptance of risk do not preserve the mandatory approval gates.
critical_evidence.correction: Require the applicable approvals before committing expenditure or implementing changed parts. If an interim authorization route is proposed, define its approving authorities, permitted activities and limits, and prohibit release of unapproved designs for production.

critical_evidence.quote_or_cell: Purchase approves and Finance and Program Manager are notified. Any price change request still needs all three approvals.
critical_evidence.why_wrong: Tier A includes cosmetic changes and follows a section covering TRSO changes, but its approval route does not require ER and Quality signoff on the revised TRSO. The price-change safeguard correctly preserves commercial approvals, but does not preserve the mandatory technical signoffs for no-cost design changes.
critical_evidence.correction: Explicitly route every revised TRSO through ER, Quality and Purchase signoff before implementation. Tier A may streamline commercial processing, but should not waive technical signoff; distinguish price-only index adjustments that do not revise the TRSO.

judgment.rationale: The submission correctly uses the approved revision-2 record and requires Finance controllers, Program Managers and Purchase to approve price changes. It also provides the requested modular cost drivers, baseline sourcing gates, nomination approvals, version history, digital-platform requirements and a practical delta-quotation approach. However, the interim letter-of-intent provision and the incomplete technical approval route for minor TRSO changes leave material governance gaps. These require substantive repair before the workflow can serve as an implementation blueprint.
